correctness.rationale: The rank-sensitive inequality follows from positivity, the exact trace identity \(\operatorname{Tr}F_{\nu,0}=d-1\), and the fact that the maximum eigenvalue is at least the mean positive eigenvalue. For an \(m\)-basis MUB subset, the trace-zero diagonal spaces are pairwise Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal, so \(F_{\nu_m,0}\) is exactly \(1/m\) times the orthogonal projector onto their direct sum. An omitted-MUB pure state and \(I/d\) induce exactly the same full outcome law while their entropies are \(0\) and \(\log d\); the midpoint constant estimator matches the resulting two-point lower bound, proving the minimax value exactly for every sample size.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp failure mode for the new frame-spread proxy: an all-but-one-MUB measurement is optimally isotropic on every operator direction it can see and has \(\kappa=1+1/d\) approaching the global optimum \(1\), yet entropy remains maximally nonidentifiable forever. This distinguishes anisotropy on the measured subspace from missing operator directions and shows that small frame spread alone cannot be interpreted as near-informational-completeness for entropy estimation. The exact rank bound also proves the example is not poorly conditioned relative to its identifiable dimension.
